---
title: "ATAC DAR with paired biological samples"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## Biological design and provenance

Use [GSE178428](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE178428):
Control and LPS at 6 h, Donor1--4, hg19. The experimental units are the four
donors measured under both conditions. Cells and technical libraries are not
additional independent biological replicates.

Prepare the series peak file and GEO cell metadata, plus these eight sample
fragment files: GSM5390937--GSM5390940 (Control) and
GSM5390957--GSM5390960 (LPS). GEO cell metadata contains capture and donor fields
but no cell-type labels. The authors' [archived Shiny data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6820097)
provides `prep/stim_ATAC_paired_cellMeta.rds`, including `pairedLabel`.
All 62,219 author-labelled barcodes occur in the 67,581-row GEO table; shared
condition, stimulus, experiment and donor fields must agree before joining.
The other 5,362 GEO cells are outside that author-labelled population.

These labels come from the study's computational RNA/ATAC pairing. They do not
turn this dataset into experimentally paired multiome measurements for LinkPeaks.

```{r select-cells}
data_dir <- "atac_dar_data"
dir.create(data_dir)
series <- "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE178nnn/GSE178428/suppl/"
for (file in c("GSE178428_PBMCs_stim_peaks.bed.gz", "GSE178428_PBMCs_stim_scATACseq_cellMeta.txt.gz")) {
  utils::download.file(paste0(series, file), file.path(data_dir, file), mode = "wb")
}
archive <- file.path(data_dir, "stimFigRShiny.zip")
utils::download.file("https://zenodo.org/api/records/6820097/files/stimFigRShiny.zip/content",
  archive, mode = "wb")
annotation_file <- "stimFigRShiny/prep/stim_ATAC_paired_cellMeta.rds"
utils::unzip(archive, files = annotation_file, exdir = data_dir)
author <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, annotation_file))
geo <- utils::read.delim(gzfile(file.path(data_dir,
  "GSE178428_PBMCs_stim_scATACseq_cellMeta.txt.gz")), row.names = 1)
stopifnot(all(rownames(author) %in% rownames(geo)))
for (field in c("Condition", "StimType", "Experiment", "Donor")) {
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(author[[field]]),
    as.character(geo[rownames(author), field])))
}
metadata <- author[author$Condition %in% c("Control_6h", "LPS_6h") &
  author$pairedLabel == "CD14_Mono", , drop = FALSE]
metadata$sample <- metadata$Experiment
metadata$condition <- factor(metadata$StimType, levels = c("Control", "LPS"))
metadata$donor <- factor(metadata$Donor)
metadata$celltype <- metadata$pairedLabel
table(metadata$donor, metadata$condition)
```

This selects 1,151 CD14 monocytes. Control has 160/181/229/302 cells across
Donor1--4; LPS has 57/21/68/133. All eight samples exceed the example's
10-cell minimum. Retain every donor rather than manufacturing replication by
splitting cells.

## Explicit interval and barcode contracts

GEO labels `GSE178428_PBMCs_stim_peaks.bed.gz` as BED. Standard BED interpretation
uses 0-based half-open intervals. There is a source discrepancy: every supplied
`end - start` is 300, whereas the methods describe 301-bp windows. Declare the
chosen interpretation and retain this limitation; do not silently shift starts
or claim an exact reconstruction of the authors' original peak ranges.

```{r peak-universe}
bed <- utils::read.delim(gzfile(file.path(data_dir,
  "GSE178428_PBMCs_stim_peaks.bed.gz")), header = FALSE)
bed <- bed[bed[[1]] == "chr1", 1:3]
names(bed) <- c("seqnames", "start", "end")
peaks <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(bed, starts.in.df.are.0based = TRUE)
GenomeInfoDb::genome(peaks) <- "hg19"
```

The worked computation uses the common 20,950 chr1 intervals, not a separate
feature universe for each sample. Its statistical family is therefore
chromosome-scoped. Never substitute the hg38 resources from the PBMC example.

Original fragment files have four columns and no read-support field. For Signac
input, retain each genuine selected record and append a fifth value of one;
this encodes record multiplicity and does not reconstruct read support. Bgzip
and index the prepared files without changing interval endpoints. Preserve the
original files and record the transformation.

Cell metadata uses `6h` in cell IDs while most fragment barcodes use `6hr`.
Use the supplied `Experiment` field plus the verified barcode suffix, not a
generic suffix-stripping rule. LPS Donor2 has `6h` inside its fragment barcodes
despite `6hr` in the filename. Verify actual barcode membership for all cells.

```{r explicit-mapping}
suffix <- sub("^.*(_BC[0-9]+_N[0-9]+)$", "\\1", rownames(metadata))
stopifnot(all(paste0(sub("_6hr_", "_6h_", metadata$Experiment, fixed = TRUE), suffix) == rownames(metadata)))
metadata$fragment_barcode <- paste0(metadata$Experiment, suffix)
sample_ids <- c(paste0("Control_6hr_Donor", 1:4, "_S1"),
  "LPS_6hr_Donor1_S1", "LPS_6h_Donor2_S1", "LPS_6hr_Donor3_S1", "LPS_6hr_Donor4_S1")
gsm <- c(5390937:5390940, 5390957:5390960)
file_ids <- sample_ids
file_ids[[6]] <- "LPS_6hr_Donor2_S1" # Verified filename; barcode prefix remains 6h.
fragment_files <- stats::setNames(file.path(data_dir, paste0("dar-", sample_ids, "-chr1.tsv.gz")), sample_ids)
maps <- lapply(names(fragment_files), function(sample) {
  cells <- metadata[metadata$Experiment == sample, , drop = FALSE]
  stats::setNames(cells$fragment_barcode, rownames(cells))
})
prepare_bap <- function(source, target, barcodes) {
  stopifnot(!file.exists(target))
  input <- gzfile(source, "rt")
  output <- file(target, "wt")
  on.exit({ close(input); close(output) })
  repeat {
    lines <- readLines(input, n = 100000, warn = FALSE)
    if (!length(lines)) break
    fields <- strsplit(lines, "\t", fixed = TRUE)
    stopifnot(all(lengths(fields) == 4L))
    keep <- vapply(fields, function(x) x[[1]] == "chr1" && x[[4]] %in% barcodes, logical(1))
    if (any(keep)) writeLines(paste0(lines[keep], "\t1"), output)
  }
}
for (i in seq_along(sample_ids)) {
  file <- paste0("GSM", gsm[i], "_", file_ids[i], ".fragments.tsv.gz")
  source <- file.path(data_dir, file)
  url <- paste0("https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/samples/GSM5390nnn/GSM", gsm[i], "/suppl/", file)
  utils::download.file(url, source, mode = "wb")
  plain <- sub("[.]gz$", "", fragment_files[i])
  prepare_bap(source, plain, unname(maps[[i]]))
  Rsamtools::bgzip(plain, dest = fragment_files[i])
  Rsamtools::indexTabix(fragment_files[i], format = "bed")
}
fragments <- Map(function(file, cells) Signac::CreateFragmentObject(file, cells = cells),
  fragment_files, maps)
matrices <- Map(function(fragment, mapping) {
  Signac::FeatureMatrix(fragment, features = peaks, cells = names(mapping))
}, fragments, maps)
counts <- do.call(cbind, unname(matrices))
atac <- scop::ReadATACData(counts, ranges = peaks, genome = "hg19",
  metadata = metadata[colnames(counts), , drop = FALSE],
  fragments = unname(fragment_files), fragment.cells = maps)
```

## Paired edgeR QL model

Within this cell type, aggregate raw peak counts by the eight sample IDs.
`~ donor + condition` accounts for donor-specific baselines. A complete named
contrast makes positive log-fold-change mean LPS relative to Control.

```{r paired-dar}
samples <- metadata[!duplicated(metadata$sample), , drop = FALSE]
design_matrix <- stats::model.matrix(~ donor + condition, samples)
contrast <- stats::setNames(rep(0, ncol(design_matrix)), colnames(design_matrix))
contrast["conditionLPS"] <- 1
atac <- scop::RunDEtest(atac,
  test.use = "edgeR", assay = "peaks", layer = "counts", feature_type = "peak",
  group.by = "celltype", sample_col = "sample", condition_col = "condition",
  group1 = "Control", group2 = "LPS", min.cells.sample = 10,
  design = ~ donor + condition, contrast = contrast,
  only.pos = FALSE, fc.threshold = 1, p.adjust.method = "BH")
model <- atac@tools$DEtest_celltype$edgeR_models$CD14_Mono
model$sample_inventory
model$design
model$contrast
complete_results <- model$full_results
```

SCOP passes the counts and design to native edgeR filtering, TMM normalization,
dispersion estimation and robust QL fitting/testing. The receipt retains raw
pseudobulk counts, true cell membership, design/contrast, normalization, tested
and filtered features, full results and backend versions. Missing combinations
are not invented as zero-count samples. This model has eight samples, five
design columns and three residual degrees of freedom.

BH correction uses the full filterByExpr-tested family before display filtering.
The compatibility column `p_val_adj` uses the requested adjustment; the explicit
`p_val_BH` remains available. Nonsignificance and a fully filtered empty result
are valid outcomes, not reasons to switch statistical engines.

## Connect DAR to motifs and export

Prepare a matching hg19 reference and the desired PWM collection explicitly:

```{r prepare-motif-reference}
fasta_gz <- file.path(data_dir, "hg19-chr1.fa.gz")
utils::download.file(
  "https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg19/chromosomes/chr1.fa.gz",
  fasta_gz, mode = "wb")
fasta <- file.path(data_dir, "hg19-chr1.fa")
Biostrings::writeXStringSet(Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(fasta_gz), fasta)
Rsamtools::indexFa(fasta)
hg19_reference <- Rsamtools::FaFile(fasta)
pfm <- TFBSTools::getMatrixSet(JASPAR2020::JASPAR2020, opts = list(
  ID = c("MA0139.1", "MA0080.5", "MA0105.4", "MA0107.1", "MA0039.4", "MA0466.2", "MA0098.3")))
```

Keep
upregulated and downregulated foregrounds separate and use the full tested
universe, not only significant peaks, as the eligible population.

```{r motif-connection}
foreground <- rownames(complete_results)[complete_results$p_val_BH < 0.05 &
  complete_results$avg_log2FC > 0]
tables <- list(DAR = complete_results, samples = model$sample_inventory)
if (length(foreground)) {
  atac <- scop::AddATACMotifs(atac, hg19_reference, pfm, genome.id = "hg19")
  enriched <- scop::RunMotifEnrichment(atac, features = foreground,
    universe = model$tested_features, n.background = 1000, seed = 19)
  enriched$receipt
  tables$motifs <- enriched$results
} else {
  message("No positive BH-significant peaks; save the complete DAR results without a motif test.")
}
scop::ExportATACResults(atac, outdir = "paired_DAR_export", assay = "peaks",
  tables = tables)
# In a fresh session:
restored <- readRDS("paired_DAR_export/object.rds")
stopifnot(scop::CheckATACData(restored)$valid)
```

Inspect the foreground first; an empty foreground is not evidence of absent TF
regulation. Motif P-values are one-sided sequence over-enrichment tests. A fold
enrichment below one does not constitute a separate under-enrichment test, and
enrichment does not demonstrate binding or causality.
